cleared.check: Task 5 for the closed or unsimulated producers: which still have no mined proof that transient storage is cleared between transactions, and what a missing clear would expose.
cleared.result: None of the four has a mined pair. The reason is the code, not the sample: the only transient words of the PoolManager that a successful transaction can leave set are the synced currency and reserves (unlock relocks at src/PoolManager.sol:113 and requires the delta count at zero at line 112). Routers sync immediately before settling, so a successful transaction that ends with an ERC-20 sync open needs an account that calls sync(X) and stops (P3, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). No account did so in 4,375 traced Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM blocks here plus 4,000 in cycle 33. The mined pair can only come from such a call, which this review may not send. Per cycle 34, a leaked sync would make a later native settle revert (src/PoolManager.sol:356) or credit the next settler with the rise of X's balance (lines 357-361), so the hazard is a freeze of one settle or a gift to the next settler, not a path for the leaving account. The producers of Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM and Arc stay covered by source and replica evidence only.

cleared.check: Task 2 (L-1358): key kinds of bor's multi-version stores and whether transient storage, logs, the access list or the refund counter are among them; read in v2.11.2, v2.11.1 and develop (core/blockstm/mvhashmap.go, mvstore.go, mvbalance_store.go, v2_executor.go, core/state/parallel_statedb*.go; the files are byte-identical across the three revisions except core/parallel_state_processor.go and core/vm/instructions.go in develop).
cleared.result: The block import path (core/blockchain.go:969-975, NewV2StateProcessor) runs V2: blockstm.MVStore keyed by a 54-byte Key of address, slot hash, subpath byte and type byte (mvhashmap.go:82-150). FlushToMVStore writes exactly five kinds: NoncePath, storage slots (NewStateKey), CodePath, CreatePath and SuicidePath (parallel_statedb.go:495-524); balances go to MVBalanceStore as per-address add and sub deltas (flushBalanceDeltas). Transient storage, logs, the access list, the refund counter and preimages are plain fields of the ParallelStateDB (parallel_statedb.go:111-118), cleared by Reset at the start of every incarnation (lines 256-281) and again by Prepare (lines 1277-1279), and SettleTo copies only nonces, storage, code, balances, logs and the account set into the final StateDB (parallel_statedb_settle.go:16-33). GetTransientState and SetTransientState touch only the local map and the journal (lines 1139-1150). The older MVHashMap (V1) holds address, state and subpath keys (Balance, Nonce, Code, Suicide; statedb.go:1036-1044) and its own comment calls V1 test-only (mvhashmap.go:429). Neither store has a transient key kind.

cleared.check: Task 2 (L-1358): one execution of a transaction by a V2 worker: where writes are buffered, when they are flushed, what an inner revert, an aborted incarnation and an invalidated reader do.
cleared.result: SetState writes localStorage and only records the key (parallel_statedb.go:1040-1065, whose comment says storage writes are always deferred). The executor calls Execute with deferWrites true and FlushToMVStore only after the whole message has run (v2_executor.go:426-455, line 447), so no other worker can see a value from inside a running frame. An inner revert undoes journal entries before the flush: revertStorage restores or deletes the localStorage entry (parallel_statedb_journal.go:73-78) and jkTransient restores the local transient map (line 56), so a reverted write is not in the flushed set. A transaction that panicked is never flushed (line 496-498). On a validation failure dispatchReexec marks the old incarnation's keys ESTIMATE, re-executes into a freshly Reset state, and CleanupEstimate deletes the entries the new incarnation did not rewrite (v2_executor.go:571-612, mvstore.go:137-169). A reader that meets an ESTIMATE falls back to the base state in incarnation 0 and waits for the writer's final version later (parallel_statedb.go:332-393); every store read is recorded and Validate rejects it unless the writer and incarnation match or the value is equal (parallel_statedb_validate.go:115-133), and the failed reader is re-executed. A wrong parallel result cannot be kept: ProcessBlock checks it against the header and falls back to the serial result (blockchain.go:1308-1420), and the block producer runs transactions one by one through core.ApplyTransaction (miner/worker.go:1713).

cleared.check: Task 2 from the shipped bor v2.11.2 amd64 binary (cycle 31 download, GitCommit a4afe5a9, sha256 prefix 6d85c1aea6d89c06): the ParallelStateDB storage path run in the cycle 32/33 x86-64 model with blockstm.(*MVStore).ReadVersionFull answering from a preloaded table (scripts/stmv.py, seed 39_1358_01): another transaction's committed value, an ESTIMATE marker with a stale value, and a committed value that is replaced after its first read. Static check of the transient path in the same binary (out/objdump-calls.txt, out/objdump-transient.txt, out/objdump-FlushToMVStore.txt).
cleared.result: 5000 sequences, 135232 SLOADs, 48973 SSTOREs, 6668 reverts, 256887 store reads (61712 committed, 36814 estimate, 14072 changing), 165632 GetCommittedState checks, 623505 write-set checks, 11171 reads of a changed entry: 0 mismatches, 0 errors. Committed values are read as the pre-state, ESTIMATE entries fall through to the base word, a changed entry is read afresh on each SLOAD of an unwritten slot (no SLOAD result cache in front of the store), and the local write set that FlushToMVStore publishes never holds a reverted write. Two planted faults are caught: a stale committed value (200 of 200 sequences) and an ESTIMATE handed back as committed (194 of 200). In the binary, (*ParallelStateDB).GetTransientState and SetTransientState call only runtime map functions and appendJournal and contain no reference to core/blockstm, opTload makes one indirect call to the StateDB interface, and FlushToMVStore calls MVStore.WriteInc at exactly five sites plus flushBalanceDeltas, matching the source. A transient word cannot be read from the store because no code path puts one there or reads one from it.

cleared.result: None. opSload and opTload in all four call StateDB.GetState and GetTransientState directly (bor core/vm/instructions.go:577-584 at v2.11.2, 616-623 at develop, core/vm/eips.go:218-226 in both; bsc instructions.go:514-520 and eips.go:201-207; libevm instructions.go:514-520 and eips.go:197-203). Behind them are the standard layers: dirtyStorage (journaled), pendingStorage (earlier transactions of the block) and originStorage (database) in bsc and libevm (state_object.go GetState and GetCommittedState), and in bor's V2 worker localStorage (journaled), the MVStore and the base state, plus committedCache for the original value only, which is fixed for a transaction and whose source read is validated. The interpreter structs of bor (v2.11.2 and develop), bsc and libevm hold no storage cache; bor develop adds a keccak result cache and a MULMOD memo, not a storage cache. The binaries agree: opSload and opTload of bor v2.11.2, bsc v1.8.2 and avalanchego v1.15.3 make only the StateDB interface call (plus libevm's Contract.Address call) and uint256 SetBytes (out/objdump-calls.txt, out/objdump-bsc-avax.txt). With no cache, the cycle 36 reentry sequences have nothing to run against.

cleared.check: Whether this theme (producers without block simulation, and a parallel executor that could share transient or reverted words between transactions) applies to the other sixteen networks.
cleared.result: It does not. Their producers are open clients whose transient clear between transactions was tested by eth_simulateV1 at the real PoolManager address in an earlier cycle (fifteen of them; OPCODES.md 'Reading from the source' row), and none commits a transaction from a parallel or speculative run without running it again (OPCODES.md 'Speculative execution' row: reth's reuse path is off by default, BNB Chain discards its prefetch runs). Avalanche has no eth_simulateV1, but its C-Chain runs libevm serially and its transient storage and journal revert ran from the v1.15.3 binary in cycle 32.

leadResults.answer: No mined pair exists on any of the four producers. Monad 2000 traced blocks, MegaETH 2249, HyperEVM 126 (replica traces, official receipts), Arc 600 blocks by calldata only (no endpoint serves traces): 0 successful transactions end with an ERC-20 sync open, so 0 pairs and nothing to replay with pyevm.py. Such a transaction needs an account to call sync(X) and stop, which no router does. The clear between transactions on these producers rests on source and replicas as before. Receipts equal the traced execution for every PoolManager transaction on Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM.

bor v2.11.2, v2.11.1 and develop have byte-identical blockstm and parallel state files. The V2 MVStore holds nonce, storage slot, code, create and suicide keys, and balances are kept as deltas in MVBalanceStore; transient storage, logs, the access list and the refund counter are per-incarnation fields that are reset, never flushed and never settled. Writes are flushed only after the whole transaction, inner reverts are undone in the local buffer first, and aborted incarnations become ESTIMATE entries that are cleaned up after re-execution. Run from the v2.11.2 binary with a preloaded store: 0 mismatches over 5,000 sequences, and two planted faults are caught. The parallel result is checked against the header and the producer builds serially.

No SLOAD or TLOAD result cache in front of the state in bor v2.11.2 or develop, bsc v1.8.2, or libevm d398bc4dbe41 (the commit avalanchego v1.15.3 pins; the lead's a335c2ecf4df is not it). Confirmed in the shipped binaries' opSload and opTload. F-165 has no counterpart in these clients.
